About the company
General Matter enriches uranium.
We are designing, building, and operating the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US.
In the process, we are restoring America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive.
Fuel drives the cost of advanced reactor electricity production, and enrichment drives the cost of the fuel that advanced reactors consume.  Reliable, low-cost enrichment is the catalyst for the nuclear Renaissance now under way.
Our mission is to make nuclear not only the cleanest and safest source of baseload power, but also the most affordable.  We believe abundant nuclear energy will lead to a post-scarcity society.
We were incubated inside Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by over a dozen of the world's top venture capital firms.
Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production.
We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency.
Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable.
About This Role
We're looking for a New Graduate Engineer with a strong interest in regulatory compliance and licensing to join our growing engineering team. You'll collaborate with experienced engineers to support licensing actions, regulatory submissions, and engagement with regulatory authorities for a nuclear fuel cycle facility. This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated graduate eager to contribute to high-reliability, highly regulated nuclear facility work.
Responsibilities
Support the preparation and review of licensing documents, including licensing applications, regulatory reports, amendment requests, and license renewal applications, in compliance with NRC requirements.
Assist in communication with regulatory agencies such as the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) and help track timely resolution of inquiries.
Support the development and implementation of strategies to obtain and maintain licenses for new and existing nuclear facilities and projects.
Perform technical evaluations under the guidance of senior engineers to help ensure compliance with applicable codes, standards, and regulations (e.g., 10 CFR).
Help monitor changes to nuclear regulations and assess their impact on operations and licensing.
Support safety analyses, environmental reports, and risk assessments to ensure regulatory compliance.
Work on documentation and technical writing to support licensing submissions and regulatory correspondence.
Collaborate with engineering, operations, legal, and environmental teams to help address licensing requirements and resolve regulatory issues.
Participate in inspections, audits, and regulatory meetings alongside senior team members.
Effectively communicate technical ideas within multidisciplinary project teams.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Nuclear Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related field (recent graduate or upcoming).
Coursework in nuclear engineering fundamentals, reactor physics, or fuel cycle systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare clear and concise technical documentation.
Strong organizational and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
Ability to communicate technical information clearly and collaboratively across disciplines.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Internship experience in nuclear licensing, regulatory affairs, or a related technical role, especially projects involving nuclear or highly regulated facilities
General familiarity with NRC regulations, including 10 CFR and related industry standards (e.g., ANSI, ASME).
Evidence of exceptional ability (prior projects, portfolio of work, completed products, etc.).
Familiarity with nuclear facility operations and safety analyses.
Exposure to interacting with regulatory agencies, such as the NRC.
Additional Requirements
Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.
